key_insight: A scale-adaptive self-supervised vision model can quantify C. elegans neuron damage across sizes and link those morphological changes to behavior for neurotoxicity screening.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve early safety screening of chemicals and support scalable, 3R-compliant alternatives to animal-based neurotoxicity testing.
method: Built CeNeuMorph, a 27,117-image confocal benchmark of dopaminergic neurons.
Developed a scale-adaptive masked image modeling strategy that learns across resolutions and patch sizes.
Combined visual embeddings with morphological descriptors to predict behavioral deficits and screen agrochemicals.
evidence_signal: The model outperformed generalist and biomedical foundation models on classification, segmentation, and detection, and the fused features predicted dopamine-dependent behavior with R² = 0.498.
watch_item: Results come from C. elegans imaging and may require careful validation before generalizing to other neuron types, species, or real-world toxicology settings.
paper_title: A Scale-adaptive Vision Model Links C. elegans Neuronal Morphology to Behavior for Neurotoxicity Assessment
